thread:
maya-platform: Heads-up — customer hit duplicate charges when a client disconnected mid-stream and then reconnected to resume. They saw the partial tokens consumed before disconnect show up again after resume. Anyone seen this in prod?

leo-runtime: Yep, saw a spike last week. Root cause looked like reservations were not committed/cleared correctly on disconnect. Two places: gateway issues that increment counters optimistically, and runtime replay path that also increments.

toni-sre: Quick Q: where do we want authoritative enforcement for per-key burst/balance? Gateway (fast reject) or runtime (single source of truth)?

sarah-p: Prefer gateway for latency + UX (fast 429s) but runtime must be authoritative to avoid double-billing. Gateway would reserve, runtime would reconcile/commit.

deb-q: Proposal: reserve tokens at stream-start by decrementing a "reserved" bucket for the key/org. On disconnect, hold reservation for a short grace window (e.g., 30s). If client resumes with same resume_token, reattach reservation and continue. If not resumed within window, release or commit depending on policy (commit = charge for what was already emitted).

leo-runtime: Implementation notes: store reservation as redis hash keyed by stream_id -> {reserved_tokens, resume_token, last_seen_ts, session_owner}. On chunk emit we decrement reserved_tokens and emit events: `stream_chunk_consumed`. On disconnect we set state=DISCONNECTED and start TTL. Resume flow must check resume_token matches and use CAS to flip state to ACTIVE.

maya-platform: Edge cases: multiple reconnect attempts (race), partial token accounting when client got 0-1 tokens before drop, and clients that open many concurrent streams to drain burst credits. Need idempotency on resume.

quota-bot: Suggest add metrics: `stream.reservation.created`, `stream.reservation.released`, `stream.reservation.committed`, `stream.resume.success`, `stream.resume.failed`, and `quota.charge.duplicate_detected`. Dashboards + alerts on `duplicate_detected > 0` for >1m.

toni-sre: Reconnect grace window tradeoffs: 30s seems reasonable for mobile flakiness. For long-polling clients we could use longer window but then reservations tie up burst credits. Consider different classes: ephemeral (30s) vs sticky (5m) reservations depending on auth/client type.

sarah-p: UX idea for Console: show "pending reservation" on keys page with hover explaining it’s held for resume window. Also expose a per-stream trace in Console -> Observability so SEs can debug double-charge complaints.

deb-q: Billing model decision: do we bill at emission or at commit? If we bill at emission, double-charge risk unless we block charges at gateway and only commit at runtime. If we bill at commit, we need reliable commit on stream end (success) and on abandon timers. I prefer commit-on-emission with reservations cleared on resume to minimize deferred accounting complexity. But caveat: must avoid gateway+runtime double increments.

leo-runtime: Technical safeguard: use monotonic `consumed_token_index` per stream persisted to durability (redis + append logs). Both gateway and runtime must use the same stream_id and check the last persisted index before incrementing. If gateway is optimistic, it must write a provisional entry and runtime's commit must be idempotent.

ops-bot: For disconnect signaling, let's standardize close codes: 4001 = client-requested, 4002 = transient-net, 4003 = server-backpressure, 4004 = resume-token-mismatch. Emit these to logs so support can filter.

maya-platform: Quick simulator I used to repro: `ws-replay --resume-token X --drop-at 12` produced double-charge when gateway retry path re-sent unacked chunks. I'll drop the script in #eng-infra.

toni-sre: Action items: 1) Design doc for reserve/commit lifecycle (deb + leo) 2) Telemetry + dashboards (quota-bot + deb) 3) Console UX mock (sarah) 4) Short-term mitigation: gate gateway optimistic increments behind a compare-and-set with runtime or reject resumes that cannot be matched.

deb-q: I'll draft the design doc and include sequence diagrams + redis schema. Will call out latency budget for gateway -> runtime reconcile (should be <100ms for common path).

maya-platform: Thanks all — sounds like we converge on reservation+reconcile model with grace windows and clearer console telemetry. @sarah-p can you slot Console mock in next sprint? :thumbsup:

sarah-p: Yup, will add to sprint planning.

quota-bot: Noted. I'll create the dashboard template and ping once it's live.

leo-runtime: I'll prototype the resume CAS logic in a branch and add unit tests for double-resume races.

maya-platform: Great — marking as working group: "stream-resume-quota". We'll do a sync if anyone hits blockers. :white_check_mark:
